# tlsresume — spec

## Maturity

**Grade:** 1 · S1 E1 A1 H1 P1 *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** ahead — OpenSSL 4.0 / BoringSSL / Go `crypto/tls` / rustls server-side resumption: TLS 1.3 tickets, PSK binders and 0-RTT, scheduled STEK rotation with a grace lifetime, TLS 1.2 tickets (RFC 5077) and a stateful session cache, as engine-agnostic parts (surveyed 2026-09-30, gaps closed 2026-10-13, OpenSSL 3.5's ticket-key handling re-read 2026-10-26); client-side resumption is `tlsclient`'s, out of scope here; live oracle `zig build interop-tlsresume` since 2026-10-26, the lead on the `**Ahead:**` line

**Ahead:** feature — scheduled STEK rotation with a grace lifetime: `maybeRotate` rotates the ticket key every `period_s` and a ticket under a rotated-out key still resumes until `lifetime_s`, then not, the key still in the ring; OpenSSL 3.5 makes one ticket key per `SSL_CTX` at `SSL_CTX_new` (`ssl/ssl_lib.c`) and replaces it only whole (`SSL_CTX_set_tlsext_ticket_keys`: every earlier ticket stops opening at once) or through an application-written ticket-key callback; rows `openssl-grace`, `openssl-expired`, `go-expired`, `openssl-k2-resume` of `zig build interop-tlsresume` (OpenSSL 3.5.5 and Go 1.26.8 clients), replayed in `interop_replay_test.zig` (measured 2026-10-26)

**Audit:** review 2026-10-28 · mutation 2026-10-28 (247/266, 19 eq) · src 55598af1eeb4113a

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-10-26 (200,000 runs per harness clean, every reach label hit, TLSRESUME_FUZZ; the ticket harness now builds distinct extension types and lifetimes up to 7 days, as `encode` requires) · ct 2026-10-26 (re-measured after the audit fixes, counts unchanged, source digests re-pinned; ctgrind: STEK + session state through StekRing seal/open/tampered open, resumption secret through derivePsk/earlySecret/binderKey/computeBinder/verifyBinder, PSK through the 0-RTT key schedule, SHA-256 and SHA-384; 2 in-file = the AES-256-GCM tag verdict in std decrypt, one per open; the PSK/binder chain and the binder compare read 0; select.selectPsk is not a row, see the harness doc) · panic 2026-10-28 (independent sweep of every pub entry point, no data-reachable panic: `SessionCache` capacity 0 asserted then dereferenced null (a disabled cache now), HKDF-Expand-Label contexts over 255 bytes (a stack overrun in ReleaseFast, now a checked panic), `SessionState.serialize` nonce over 255 (`NonceTooLong`), clock and lifetime arithmetic in `StekRing`/`StrikeRegister`/`SessionCache`/`selectPsk` overflow-free, `depthFor` checked; state + ticket 200,000 driver runs clean after it)

**Performance:** ref 0.86–0.91× OpenSSL 3.5.5 EVP · fastest 1.18× aws-lc-rs 1.18.0, rustls's provider (same recipe on each, byte-identical output: AES-256-GCM ticket seal/open, HKDF/HMAC-SHA256 PSK-binder chain; neither has a standalone resumption API; the worst row is the binder chain, std SHA-256 against aws-lc's) (measured 2026-10-26)

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** yes

Design and threat notes below. Usage: see `./README.md`. Attribution/provenance: this
module's own `./NOTICE` (module-local, as `dtls`'s is).

**Where we are ahead:** the only Zig code with server-side TLS 1.3 resumption pieces, and engine-agnostic by design (pure functions over caller bytes; bounded fail-closed strike register; constant-time binder compare); binder, NewSessionTicket and the 0-RTT key schedule are byte-exact against RFC 8448 §3/§4, including the real encrypted early-data record. **Where we are behind:** client side (out of scope: the TLS client is `tlsclient`); it is a set of parts rather than a resumption feature, and the engine has to be written around it; live-peer interop through its own oracle (`zig build interop-tlsresume`: OpenSSL and Go clients against `tlsserver` as the engine) and through the consumer `tlsserver`'s interop (OpenSSL, Go, BoGo), and the web-server consumer does not call `psk`/`select`/`earlydata`/`replay`/`cache` (the web-server consumer's engine has its own binder logic and refuses early data). Provided besides the TLS 1.3 parts: scheduled STEK rotation (`RotationPolicy`, `maybeRotate`, `expire`, `openAt`, `depthFor`), TLS 1.2 tickets (`ticket12`), stateful session cache (`SessionCache`).

## What this is, in one paragraph

Server-side TLS 1.3 session-ticket resumption (RFC 8446), engine-agnostic:
the TLS engine (this repo's `dtls` targets DTLS 1.3 PSK mode and explicitly
declares resumption out of scope; the vendored `ianic/tls.zig` implements
only the CLIENT side of resumption) passes in transcript-hash bytes and
already-negotiated secrets, and this module returns derived PSKs,
binder-verify decisions, ticket wire bytes, and STEK-sealed ticket blobs. It
never parses a ClientHello, never owns a handshake state machine, never
touches a socket.

## RFC 8446 sections covered, one line each

| Section | What / why |
|---|---|
| §4.2.11 | `pre_shared_key` extension shape: a list of `PskIdentity` (opaque identity + `obfuscated_ticket_age`) and a separate, positionally-aligned list of binders — `select.zig`'s `OfferedIdentity`/`selectPsk` model this split directly. |
| §4.2.11.1 | Obfuscated ticket age: `obfuscated_ticket_age = (age_ms + ticket_age_add) mod 2^32`; the server recomputes and freshness-checks it — `replay.zig`'s `obfuscateAge`/`deobfuscateAge`/`withinFreshnessWindow` (all REAL, no crypto). |
| §4.2.11.2 | The PSK binder: `HMAC(finished_key, Transcript-Hash(Truncate(ClientHello)))`, `finished_key` derived from `binder_key` — `psk.zig`'s `computeBinder`/`verifyBinder` (REAL; the single highest-severity item in this module). |
| §4.6.1 | `NewSessionTicket` wire shape (`ticket_lifetime`/`ticket_age_add`/`ticket_nonce`/`ticket`/`extensions`, incl. `early_data`) — `ticket.zig` (REAL, KAT-validated against the actual RFC 8448 §3 wire bytes). |
| §4.2.10 | `early_data`: the `max_early_data_size` advertisement lives in `ticket.zig` (`maxEarlyDataSize`/`earlyDataExtension`); the 0-RTT key derivation the advertisement enables is `earlydata.zig` (REAL, see the 0-RTT section below). |
| §7.1 | The key-schedule labels this module needs: `PSK = HKDF-Expand-Label(resumption_master_secret, "resumption", ticket_nonce, Hash.length)`, `Early Secret = HKDF-Extract(0, PSK)`, `binder_key = Derive-Secret(early_secret, "res binder", "")` — `psk.zig`'s `derivePsk`/`earlySecret`/`binderKey` (all REAL) — plus the early branch `Derive-Secret(early_secret, "c e traffic"/"e exp master", ClientHello)` — `earlydata.zig` (REAL). |
| §7.3 | Traffic-key calculation for early-data records: `key = HKDF-Expand-Label(secret, "key", "", key_len)`, `iv = …("iv", "", 12)` — `earlydata.zig`'s `earlyTrafficKeyIv` (REAL). |
| §8 / §8.1 / §8.2 | Anti-replay for single-use PSKs / 0-RTT: single-use tickets (chosen shape here), ClientHello recording, freshness-only — `replay.zig`'s `StrikeRegister` (REAL, bounded fail-closed eviction). |

## Design & invariants

**Layered like `dtls`/`noise` (this repo's other TLS-family modules).** The codecs and bookkeeping
(`ticket`, `ticket12`, `cache`, `stek` rotation, `replay` arithmetic) are allocation-light with one byte layout each,
matched against real wire traces; the crypto core (AEAD seal/open, the HKDF/HMAC chains, the strike register,
selection) carries the security-critical judgment calls (nonce-reuse policy, constant-time compares, replay-window
sizing). `root.zig`'s module doc table lists each file.

**Engine-agnostic, no owned state machine.** Every function takes
already-computed bytes (transcript hashes, secrets, wall-clock readings) as
parameters; nothing here calls a clock, generates randomness, or reads a
socket. This mirrors `dtls.keyschedule`/`dtls.aead` (pure functions over
caller-supplied bytes) rather than `dtls.Connection` — there is no
`tlsresume.Connection` because this module is not a transport, it is the
resumption *policy + crypto* seam a transport-owning engine calls into.

**STEK ticket-blob layout is `tlsresume`'s own choice, not RFC-mandated.**
RFC 8446 §4.6.1 explicitly leaves `ticket`'s contents to the server
("entirely up to the server"). This module picks:

```
ticket blob  := key_id(1) || nonce(12) || ciphertext(N) || tag(16)    (stek.zig)
plaintext    := resumption_master_secret(32|48) || nonce_len(1) || ticket_nonce
             || issued_at_ms(8, BE i64) || ticket_age_add(4, BE u32)  (select.zig's SessionState)
```

`stek.zig` itself is agnostic to what it seals (any `[]const u8`);
`select.zig`'s `SessionState(rms_len)` defines the canonical minimal
plaintext this module's own `selectPsk` expects, documented as a REQUIRED
PREFIX so an engine can append its own extra fields (ALPN, negotiated
group, early-data limits, ...) after it without breaking `parse`.

## Rotation, TLS 1.2 tickets and the session cache

- **Rotation (`stek.zig`).** `RotationPolicy{period_s = 24 h, lifetime_s = 7 d}` mirrors Go `crypto/tls`
  (rotate daily, accept 7 days) and rustls' `Ticketer`. `needsRotation` is `now - installed >= period`;
  `maybeRotate` rotates with id = previous active `+% 1` (0 for an empty ring) then `expire`s; `expire`
  wipes non-active slots with `installed + lifetime <= now` (the active key is never expired, so a stalled
  rotation cannot leave the server unable to seal); `openAt` also refuses an over-lifetime key still in the
  ring (including an overdue active key). `rotate` wipes the evicted slot's key before overwriting.
  `depth` must be at least `depthFor(policy)` (= ⌈lifetime/period⌉ + 1, 8 for the Go defaults) for the grace
  window to be honoured by the ring itself; `DefaultRing` (3) keeps a key for about two periods only.
- **TLS 1.2 tickets (`ticket12.zig`).** RFC 5077 §3.3 body (`u32 lifetime_hint; opaque ticket<0..2^16-1>`;
  a zero-length ticket is the §3.3 withdrawal, `isWithdrawal`) and the §3.2 extension (type 35). The ticket is a `StekRing.seal` blob; the engine serializes its own 1.2
  state (master secret, suite, ...) as for 1.3. The ring's `key_id||nonce||ct||tag` is one AES-256-GCM AEAD with the id as
  AAD (RFC 5077 §4's CBC+HMAC layout is not adopted, see *What is deliberately not done*).
- **Session cache (`cache.zig`).** Fixed-size entries, one allocation, single owner. O(capacity) scan with a
  full pass and `timing_safe.eql` on padded ids (ids are bearer secrets); oldest-by-insertion eviction;
  timeout `now - stored >= timeout_s`; `take` is the single-use redemption RFC 8446 §8.1 needs. Capacity 0 is a
  disabled cache: `put` stores nothing, every lookup misses.

## Hardening decisions in the API

- `selectPsk`: with a strike register the freshness window applied is at most `strikeFreshnessCap(register window)`
  (half of it), also when the caller passes none; `identities.len != binders.len` is `error.BinderMismatch`; a ticket
  that was opened and not selected is wiped from `open_scratch`, the selected one is the caller's to wipe once done with
  the session.
- `ticket.NewSessionTicket.encode` returns `error.InvalidField` for a `ticket_lifetime` over 7 days
  (`max_ticket_lifetime_s`), a nonce over 255 bytes, an empty or over-long ticket, an over-long extension or block, or an
  extension type twice; `decode` refuses an extension type twice with `error.Malformed` (RFC 8446 §4.2).
- `StekRing(depth)`: a depth over 256 is a compile error (key ids are `u8`); `findKey` returns the newest key with an
  id; `wipe()` clears every key (a ring is a plain value: a copy is a copy of the keys).
- `SessionState.serialize` refuses a nonce over 255 bytes (`NonceTooLong`); an HKDF-Expand-Label context over 255 bytes
  is a checked panic (`psk.zig`), not a stack overrun.

## Threat model

- **Binder forgery (highest severity).** `psk.computeBinder`/`verifyBinder`
  (RFC 8446 §4.2.11.2) is the one check that proves the client actually
  possesses the PSK derived from a specific prior connection's
  `resumption_master_secret` — skip it, or compare it with a variable-time
  `std.mem.eql`, and an attacker who merely observed a ticket on the wire
  (tickets are NOT confidential in transit — they are bearer tokens
  protected only by the STEK seal) can splice it into their own connection.
  `verifyBinder` compares with `std.crypto.timing_safe.eql`, and the
  `computeBinder` HMAC math is KAT-validated byte-exact against RFC 8448 §4
  — the constant-time-compare invariant is locked in at the type-signature
  level, not left to callers to remember.
- **Ticket replay.** A captured ticket + its (also captured, or freshly
  computed by the attacker if they also have the PSK) binder is fully
  reusable unless the server enforces something from RFC 8446 §8 — this
  module's chosen shape is `replay.StrikeRegister`'s single-use strike
  register (§8.1), implemented with a bounded fail-closed eviction policy
  (see `replay.zig`'s module doc); a server that
  skips this by policy (accepting resumption PSKs multiple times, common
  for the NON-0-RTT case — RFC 8446 only mandates single-use enforcement
  for 0-RTT/early-data acceptance, §8) is not "wrong" per se, but the type
  exists so a server that does want it has a real seam to call.
- **STEK compromise / rotation.** `stek.StekRing`'s bounded `depth` limits
  the blast radius of one leaked key (only tickets sealed under that one
  rotation slot are affected) and enables forward-secrecy-by-rotation (an
  operator that rotates keys and discards old ones makes tickets sealed
  under the discarded key permanently unopenable, i.e. a coarse-grained
  ticket lifetime ceiling independent of `ticket_lifetime`). `rotate`'s
  caller supplies the key material — this module never generates key bytes
  itself, so it carries no CSPRNG-quality risk of its own; that
  responsibility sits with the engine, consistent with this repo's
  no-hidden-globals rule (CONVENTIONS.md §2).
- **Const-time compare, generally.** Every crypto-critical value compare in this module uses
  `std.crypto.timing_safe.eql`, never `std.mem.eql`: the binder (`psk.verifyBinder`) and the session-cache id
  (`cache.zig`, over padded ids). The AEAD tag verdict is the AEAD's own, inside `stek.open`.
- **Ticket-age spoofing.** `replay.withinFreshnessWindow` bounds how far a
  client's claimed `obfuscated_ticket_age` may diverge from the server's own
  elapsed-time measurement (RFC 8446 §4.2.11.1) — this is a DoS/early-data
  replay mitigant, not a confidentiality boundary (a client can always claim
  ANY age within the window; the point is bounding how large a replay
  window an attacker gets, not proving a specific age).
- **Residual risk: one ring for two purposes.** The ticket AAD is the key id alone and `SessionState` does not record
  its hash length, so one ring shared by TLS 1.2 and 1.3 tickets, or by SHA-256 and SHA-384 sessions, relies on the
  engine's `Filter` (suite in the tail) to refuse a foreign state; otherwise such a ticket may end in `BinderMismatch`
  instead of a full handshake (only for the client that offers it). Use one ring per purpose and hash; documented on
  `seal` and `SessionState`.
- **Residual risk: full strike register.** A register full of live entries rescans per new identifier (documented on
  `checkAndMark`).

## Implementation notes (`psk`, `stek`, `replay`, `select`)

What each function does and the decisions it carries:

1. `psk.zig: earlySecret` — RFC 8446 §7.1 `HKDF-Extract(salt = 0^Hash.length,
   IKM = PSK)` via `Hkdf.extract`. KAT: RFC 8448 §4 early_secret.
2. `psk.zig: derivePsk` — RFC 8446 §7.1/§4.6.1
   `HKDF-Expand-Label(resumption_master_secret, "resumption", ticket_nonce,
   Hash.length)` via `std.crypto.tls.hkdfExpandLabel` (its hardcoded
   `"tls13 "` prefix is exactly right here). KAT: RFC 8448 §4 PSK.
3. `psk.zig: binderKey` — RFC 8446 §7.1 `Derive-Secret(early_secret, "res
   binder", "")` — the label is `"res binder"`, NOT `"ext binder"`
   (external-PSK case, which this module does not implement — see
   `dtls.keyschedule.binderKey` for that sibling case). KAT: RFC 8448 §4
   binder_key.
4. `psk.zig: computeBinder` — RFC 8446 §4.2.11.2: `finished_key =
   HKDF-Expand-Label(binder_key, "finished", "", Hash.length)`, then
   `HMAC(finished_key, transcript_hash)`. **Highest-severity function in
   the module** — see the threat model above. KAT: RFC 8448 §4
   finished_key + binder, byte-exact.
5. `stek.zig: StekRing(depth).seal` / `.open` — AES-256-GCM over the blob
   layout above, with the 1-byte key id authenticated as the AEAD
   associated data (a blob cannot be re-pointed at a different ring slot).
   The AEAD is `stek.Aead` = `aesgcm.Aes256Gcm` (the zig-libs `aesgcm` module). Fresh nonce per seal is caller-supplied (no-owned-RNG design); any tag
   mismatch is the typed `error.DecryptionFailed`, never a panic on
   attacker-controlled bytes.
6. `replay.zig: StrikeRegister.checkAndMark` — RFC 8446 §8/§8.1 single-use
   anti-replay: an identifier repeats within `window_ms` -> reject;
   capacity-bounded with expired-entry eviction; a register full of live
   entries fail-closes on new identifiers (rejecting resumption only forces
   a full handshake — never evicts a live entry, which would re-open its
   replay window). See `replay.zig`'s module doc for the full policy.
7. `select.zig: selectPsk` — composes all of the above (unseal with
   `openAt` under the caller's `RotationPolicy`, so a key past its lifetime
   never opens a ticket even if `expire` was not called → parse → session
   age cap of 7 days, RFC 8446 §4.6.1 → freshness → derive PSK → verify binder → strike register → first match
   wins). The binder is verified BEFORE the strike register is marked, so a
   forged binder can never consume a real ticket's single-use slot (no
   attacker-driven DoS of the legitimate client's resumption).

## 0-RTT early-data key derivation (`earlydata.zig`)

The early-data branch of the RFC 8446 §7.1 key schedule, so a resuming client's 0-RTT records can be
protected/opened before the handshake completes.

- `clientEarlyTrafficSecret` = `Derive-Secret(early_secret, "c e traffic",
  ClientHello)`; `earlyExporterMasterSecret` = `Derive-Secret(early_secret,
  "e exp master", ClientHello)`. Both take the transcript hash of the
  **complete** ClientHello (binders included) — deliberately distinct from
  `psk.computeBinder`'s **truncated**-ClientHello hash; the doc comments and
  KATs pin this distinction because it is the one wrong input a caller can
  plausibly pass.
- `earlyTrafficKeyIv` = the §7.3 record-protection pair (`"key"`/`"iv"`
  labels, 12-byte IV; key_len 16 or 32 per the §B.4 suites; SHA-256 and
  SHA-384 via the comptime `Hkdf` parameter, as everywhere in this module).
- `EarlyDataContext(Hkdf, key_len).derive(psk, ch_hash)` — one-call
  convenience: PSK → `early_secret` (REUSES `psk.earlySecret`) →
  `client_early_traffic_secret` → key/iv.
- What it does NOT own (cross-referenced, not reimplemented): the
  `max_early_data_size` advertisement is `ticket.zig`'s (§4.2.10), and the
  anti-replay defense 0-RTT REQUIRES (§8, §2.3 — early data is replayable
  without it) is `replay.StrikeRegister` + `withinFreshnessWindow`. Deriving
  early keys without wiring those is a replay vulnerability, not a working
  configuration.

**KAT sourcing for 0-RTT — official, not self-consistency:** RFC 8448 §4
("Resumed 0-RTT Handshake") is itself a full 0-RTT trace and carries
byte-exact vectors for the entire early branch: the `"tls13 c e traffic"`
and `"tls13 e exp master"` derivations (complete-ClientHello hash
`08ad0f…`), the early write key/iv, and even the client's actual encrypted
early-data record (payload `"ABCDEF"`). `earlydata.zig`'s tests assert all
of these byte-exact — including AEAD-opening the trace's real record with
the derived key/iv and a seal/open round-trip in the other direction. The
one thing RFC 8448 does NOT carry is a SHA-384 0-RTT vector (its trace is
TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 only), so the SHA-384/key_len-32 test asserts
internal consistency (manual chain == convenience type, AES-256-GCM
seal/open round-trip) rather than an external byte-exact target — the same
honest split `psk.zig`'s SHA-384 test already makes.

## KAT sourcing (RFC 8448)

`psk.zig`'s, `earlydata.zig`'s, and `replay.zig`'s KAT constants are
extracted directly from <https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8448> §3
("Simple 1-RTT Handshake", whose NewSessionTicket trace `ticket.zig`
decodes byte-for-byte) and §4 ("Resumed 0-RTT Handshake", whose
PSK/binder-key/finished-key/binder chain `psk.zig` targets and whose
early-traffic-secret/early-key-iv/encrypted-early-record trace
`earlydata.zig` targets). This is the SAME source `dtls.keyschedule.zig` already
uses for its own (external-PSK, `"ext binder"`) binder KAT — the
resumption-PSK chain here diverges from that one exactly at the `"res
binder"` vs `"ext binder"` label, per RFC 8446 §7.1's two separate PSK
binder-key derivations.

## Verification

Run: `scripts/modtest tlsresume`; live oracle: `zig build interop-tlsresume` (`tools/interop.zig`, `tlsserver` as the engine
through `interop_deps`); deterministic fuzz: `TLSRESUME_FUZZ=<runs>[,<first seed>]`; constant time:
`scripts/checks/ctgrind.sh tlsresume`.

- **KAT:** RFC 8448 §3 (`NewSessionTicket` wire bytes) and §4 (PSK, early secret, binder key, finished key, binder,
  the 0-RTT early traffic secret, key/iv and the real encrypted early-data record, opened with the derived key), byte-exact
  in `ticket`, `psk`, `earlydata`; STEK seal/open; strike-register policy; `selectPsk` end to end. RFC 8448 carries no
  SHA-384 0-RTT vector, so that test asserts internal consistency (manual chain == convenience type, AES-256-GCM seal/open
  round trip).
- **Self-consistency:** issue a ticket, seal it, resume against the same process's `selectPsk`, and assert the PSK
  equals the one derived independently from the same `resumption_master_secret` and `ticket_nonce`.
- **Live oracle** (`tools/interop.zig`): OpenSSL 3.5 `s_client` and Go's crypto/tls (`tools/go_peer`) resume against
  tickets sealed by a `StekRing` this program rotates: both hashes, HelloRetryRequest, 0-RTT taken, replayed (strike
  register) and refused for age skew, rotation grace and key expiry, the stateful `SessionCache`, and Go's TLS 1.2
  client against OpenSSL's and Go's TLS 1.2 servers through `ticket12`. `-- --capture` writes `src/interop_vectors.zig`,
  which `interop_replay_test.zig` replays through `selectPsk`/`EarlyDataContext`/`ticket12` in every lane (real OpenSSL
  and Go resuming ClientHellos, and a 0-RTT record).
- **Fuzz:** driver harnesses `tlsresume-ticket` (`NewSessionTicket` decode) and `tlsresume-state` (`SessionState` parse),
  each with a generated-record overlay (serialize/encode then parse/decode must round-trip; every truncation and a
  trailing octet must be refused).
- **Dead-stack rule:** `src/stackprobe_test.zig` probes every entry point (testkit engine).
- **ctgrind:** `src/ctgrind_harness.zig` (STEK and session state through seal/open, the resumption secret through the
  PSK/binder chain, the PSK through the 0-RTT key schedule, SHA-256 and SHA-384); the rows are the Hardening line's.
- **Audit:** the card's `**Audit:**` line is the current score, cumulative over the last whole-module mutation run and
  the delta runs after it.

## Performance

`zig build bench-tlsresume` (`tools/bench.zig`, `BENCH_ROUNDS`, ReleaseFast) times AES-256-GCM ticket seal/open and the
HKDF/HMAC-SHA256 PSK-binder chain against OpenSSL EVP (`tools/c_bench`) and aws-lc-rs (`tools/rust_fast_bench`), the same
recipe on each; neither has a standalone resumption API. The card's Performance line carries the figures. The binder
chain is generic over the caller's `Hkdf`/`Hmac`, so an engine can plug a faster SHA-256.

## What is deliberately not done

- **Client-side resumption** — `tlsclient`'s; this module is the server side.
- **A handshake engine** — no ClientHello parsing, no state machine, no socket, no clock, no RNG: the engine passes
  bytes in (see *What this is*).
- **External-PSK binders** (`"ext binder"`) — only the resumption chain (`"res binder"`) is implemented; the sibling
  case is `dtls.keyschedule.binderKey`.
- **RFC 5077 §4's recommended CBC+HMAC ticket layout** — the ring's blob is one AES-256-GCM AEAD with the key id as AAD.
- **A purpose byte in the ticket AAD** (see the residual risk "one ring for two purposes" in the threat model) — it
  would change every sealed byte and the consumer's captured vectors; a ring per purpose and hash is the documented
  answer.

## Backlog / deferred

None open.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

- **Class A** — wire/interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it.
- **Oracle EXTERNAL** — published vectors, goldens captured from a foreign implementation, or a test run against a live foreign peer.

**What the tests actually contain.** RFC 8448 KAT byte-exact: ticket/psk-binder/earlydata/replay real vectors
